es.summary: Anticoagulante oral que inhibe la síntesis hepática de los factores de coagulación dependientes de la vitamina K.
key_points: Se monitoriza mediante INR; rango terapéutico 2‑3 para la mayoría de indicaciones.
Interacción importante con alimentos ricos en vitamina K y muchos fármacos.
Riesgo principal: sangrado, especialmente gastrointestinal y intracraneal.
Requiere educación al paciente sobre cumplimiento y signos de sangrado.

mechanism: Bloquea la enzima epóxido reductasa, impidiendo la reciclación de la vitamina K.
Disminuye la gamma‑carboxilación de los factores II, VII, IX y X.
Reduce la capacidad de la sangre para formar coágulos.
indications: Prevención y tratamiento de trombosis venosa profunda (TVP) y embolia pulmonar (EP).
Prevención de eventos tromboembólicos en fibrilación auricular.
Profilaxis de tromboembolismo en prótesis valvulares mecánicas.
contraindications: Hemorragia activa o riesgo alto de sangrado.
adverse_effects: Serious: sangrado intracraneal, hemorragia gastrointestinal masiva.
interactions: Aumenta INR con antibióticos (p. ej., trimetoprim‑sulfametoxazol).
Disminuye INR con inductores de CYP450 (p. ej., rifampicina).
Alimentos ricos en vitamina K (espinaca, brócoli) reducen efecto.
AINEs y antitrombóticos potencian el riesgo de sangrado.
nursing_care: Obtener INR antes de iniciar y luego 2‑3 veces por semana hasta estabilizar.
Retener la dosis si INR > 4 y notificar al médico.
Evaluar signos de sangrado: hematuria, melena, sangrado gingival.
Mantener registro de alimentos ricos en vitamina K y educar al paciente.
No administrar si presenta hemorragia activa; notificar inmediatamente.
patient_teaching: Tomar la warfarina a la misma hora cada día.
Informar cualquier cambio en la dieta, especialmente verduras de hoja verde.
Reportar sangrado inusual, moretones grandes o sangre en la orina.
Acudir a controles de INR según lo programado.
antidote_overdose: Vitamina K1 (fitomenadiona) vía oral o IV según gravedad.
Concentrados de protrombina (PCC) o plasma fresco congelado para sangrado grave.

outcomes: Control del sangrado: sin evidencia de hemorragia activa durante la hospitalización.
INR dentro del rango terapéutico (2‑3) en al menos 80% de los controles.

interventions.action: Obtener y registrar INR antes de cada dosis y según orden médica.
interventions.rationale: Permite ajustar la dosis y prevenir sangrado excesivo.

interventions.action: Evaluar signos de sangrado cada turno (orina, heces, mucosas).
interventions.rationale: Detección temprana de hemorragia para intervención oportuna.

interventions.action: Educar al paciente sobre dieta y medicamentos que alteran INR.
Retener o reducir la dosis si INR > 4 y notificar al médico.
Mantener lista de contactos de emergencia y protocolos de reversión (Vitamina K, PCC).
interventions.rationale: Facilita respuesta rápida ante sangrado severo.

en.summary: Oral anticoagulant that inhibits hepatic synthesis of vitamin K–dependent clotting factors.
key_points: Monitored via INR; therapeutic range 2‑3 for most indications.
Important interaction with vitamin K–rich foods and many drugs.
Primary risk: bleeding, especially gastrointestinal and intracranial.
Requires patient education on adherence and bleeding signs.

mechanism: Blocks the enzyme epoxide reductase, preventing vitamin K recycling.
Reduces gamma‑carboxylation of factors II, VII, IX, and X.
Decreases blood’s ability to form clots.
indications: Prevention and treatment of deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE).
Prevention of thromboembolic events in atrial fibrillation.
Prophylaxis of thromboembolism in mechanical valve prostheses.
contraindications: Active hemorrhage or high bleeding risk.
adverse_effects: Serious: intracranial hemorrhage, massive gastrointestinal bleeding.
interactions: Decreases INR with CYP450 inducers (e.g., rifampin).
Vitamin K–rich foods (spinach, broccoli) reduce effect.
NSAIDs and antithrombotics increase bleeding risk.
nursing_care: Obtain INR before starting and then 2‑3 times per week until stable.
Hold dose if INR > 4 and notify provider.
Assess for bleeding signs: hematuria, melena, gingival bleeding.
Maintain a record of vitamin K–rich foods and educate the patient.
Do not administer if active bleeding; notify immediately.
patient_teaching: Take warfarin at the same time each day.
Report any dietary changes, especially green leafy vegetables.
Report unusual bleeding, large bruises, or blood in urine.
antidote_overdose: Vitamin K1 (phytonadione) orally or IV as severity dictates.
Prothrombin complex concentrates (PCC) or fresh frozen plasma for severe bleeding.

outcomes: No evidence of active hemorrhage during hospitalization.
INR within therapeutic range (2‑3) in at least 80% of checks.

interventions.action: Obtain and record INR before each dose and as ordered.
interventions.rationale: Allows dose adjustment and prevents excessive bleeding.

interventions.action: Assess for bleeding signs each shift (urine, stool, mucous membranes).
interventions.rationale: Early detection of hemorrhage for timely intervention.

interventions.action: Educate patient on diet and medications that alter INR.
Hold or reduce dose if INR > 4 and notify provider.
Maintain emergency contact list and reversal protocols (Vitamin K, PCC).
interventions.rationale: Facilitates rapid response to severe bleeding.

summary.0.quote: Inhibits the production of vitamin K, which is needed for synthesis of clotting factors II, VII, IX, and X

key_points.0.quote: The therapeutic goal INR varies per indication but is usually 2–3.

key_points.1.quote: Warfarin has numerous drug and food interactions.

key_points.2.quote: The major side effect of all anticoagulant medications is bleeding complications.

key_points.3.quote: Because of all the extra monitoring and food and drug interaction, warfarin requires in-depth client education.

sections.mechanism.2.quote: They work in different parts of the coagulation cascade to decrease the propensity of the blood to form a clot.

sections.indications.0.quote: It is an oral drug used for the treatment of DVT (deep vein thrombosis)/PE (pulmonary embolism), stroke prevention in atrial fibrillation, and thromboembolism prophylaxis after hip arthroplasty.

sections.indications.1.quote: Prophylaxis and treatment of thromboembolic complications associated with atrial fibrillation and/or cardiac valve replacement
